The key fact about "MAX-A-MILLION" is how its thirteen prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward small, frequent prizes. Games built like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

If you play "MAX-A-MILLION" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
985.headline: What type of game it is

988.body:
The top prize count on "Emerald 10's" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has two of five top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Today's free summary of "Emerald 10's" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
988.headline: Good news: no big claims

990.body:
"LADY LUCK" has had no $20,000 top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

Everything above about "LADY LUCK" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
990.headline: Six months, no top prize claimed

992.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$2 MILLION VAULT" have been sold. The game is well into its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

Tomorrow's count on "$2 MILLION VAULT" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
992.headline: How far along this game is

993.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$5,000 Triple Play" are sold. The top prize count has held, with three of six still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Everything here about "$5,000 Triple Play" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through October 16.
993.headline: Top prizes are still left

994.body:
The most common win left on "$25,000 Triple Play" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $3,000, and three of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Today's free summary of "$25,000 Triple Play" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
994.headline: A close look at the prizes

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" has 176,751 prizes of $10 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $5,000 prize, with two left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Tomorrow's count on "$200,000 Triple Play" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
995.headline: The prize table, line by line

996.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "$1,000,000 Triple Play" have been sold. The game is in the second half of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

If "$1,000,000 Triple Play" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
